To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a drawing of a graph with axis-parallel rectangle representations of all cuts exists if and only if a rooted cactus model of the cuts exists, and that such a drawing can be constructed in linear time if it exists.

the family of cuts that can be represented by axis-parallel rectangles is the family of minimum cuts, and that there is an efficient algorithm to decide whether a family of cuts can be represented by such rectangles and, if so, to construct such a representation.

the families of all minimum cuts, all maximum cuts, and all odd cuts are the only families of cuts of a given graph that admit a drawing such that every cut of the family is represented by an augmented axis-parallel rectangle.

the following questions. What families of cuts of a given graph admit a drawing in a certain way? What is the complexity of deciding this?
the question: what is the complexity of deciding whether there exists an augmented drawing of a graph in which every cut of the graph is represented by a given family of cuts?

the family of all cuts is the only family of cuts that admits a drawing in which the cuts are represented by simple closed curves and the graph is represented as a straight-line graph.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the families that can be represented by axis-parallel rectangles are the same as the families that can have a drawing with simple closed curves that are axis-parallel rectangles, and the latter are exactly those that can be rooted in a cactus model.
the families of axis-parallel rectangles are the most general families of cuts that are closed under intersection and have the property that the cuts can be represented by a simple geometric object.
the families of minimum cuts and of all cuts that have a cacti representation are the two families of cuts that can be drawn with axis-parallel cuts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of an axis-parallel representation of a family of cut is equivalent to the existence of a certain rooted cactus model.
a family of cuts is not necessarily more complex if the cuts are represented by non-simple curves.
